title: The Olympic Marathon Runner Who Took a Car | 1904 St. Louis
topic: The Olympic Marathon Runner Who Took a Car
format_note: User-specified ~35 s historical Short (75 words, 33.3 s). Overrides the 50-60 s explainer targets on purpose.
mechanism: In the 1904 St. Louis marathon Fred Lorz quit, rode in a car, ran the last stretch when it broke down and crossed first; he was disqualified once the ride came out, and exhausted Thomas Hicks, held up by his trainers, was the real winner.

beats.hook: Running shoes cut to a spinning car wheel: Lorz riding in a car. A CAR?!
beats.story: Lorz labours on the hot dusty road, stops, doubled over
beats.rise: A car pulls up, he hops in, cruises smugly; it breaks down and he runs into the stadium and breaks the tape to cheers
beats.twist: The cheering stops dead; an official marches in pointing; DISQUALIFIED is chalked on the board
beats.mechanism: The real winner Thomas Hicks staggers in held up by two men
beats.ending: Hicks held up at the line, Lorz alone; FIRST ACROSS ≠ WINNER

seed.what: The car (and its driver) that Lorz rides in

characters.look: Runner: white singlet, bib 31, navy shorts, dark hair
Runner: white singlet, bib 20, white shorts
Bearded driver in a duster coat and bowler
Official in a dark suit and bowler, beard
Two trainers in white shirts, a boater and a bowler
Spectators in boaters, bowlers and wide hats

gags.what: Lorz hops into the passing car and waves smugly as it drives off
The engine bursts in steam, the car lurches and Lorz is thrown forward
He bursts through the tape and the crowd's hats go flying
Hicks's knees buckle and the two trainers haul him up
